title: Unicode Standard 18.0.0, Chapter 16: Southeast Asia-I — Khmer
scope: Khmer subscript consonant and independent-vowel encoding; orthographic-syllable component order; structural treatment of COENG plus following subscript character

title: Unicode Standard Annex #29, Unicode 18.0.0, Revision 49
scope: Default extended grapheme-cluster and word-boundary rules; documentation that Khmer word boundaries require tailoring and that script-specific orthographic syllable units may require additional tailoring

title: Unicode Standard 17.0.0, Chapter 16: South and Southeast Asian Scripts — Khmer
scope: Khmer encoding structure, consonant registers, coeng, vowel signs, independent vowels, signs, visual/logical order

title: Richard Ishida, Khmer (Cambodian) Orthography Notes
scope: Modern Khmer orthography, consonant registers, vowel-sign behavior, IPA-oriented descriptive phonology, syllable structure

title: The Standard Khmer vowel system: An acoustic study
scope: Phnom Penh acoustic vowel system; 21 source-reported monophthongs and 13 diphthongs; class/register and coda effects
method: 21 speakers screened with 168 items; four speakers (two female) selected for acoustic analysis; 61 lexical items, three formal-reading repetitions
limitations: No exhaustive consonant-series × vowel × coda cross-table; /i/ omitted from acoustic sample; Standard Khmer and Phnom Penh contrasts differ; source transcription is not project gold

title: The Main features of Cambodian Pronunciation
journal: Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies 14(1):149–174
scope: historically important description of Khmer register and pronunciation

title: Incipient tonogenesis in Phnom Penh Khmer: Acoustic and perceptual studies
scope: Phnom Penh production and perception; f0, aspiration/VOT, voice quality and vowel-quality cues associated with colloquial /r/-loss

title: Incipient tonogenesis in Phnom Penh Khmer: Computational studies
scope: phonologization of f0 and breathy phonation following /r/-loss

title: Sound changes following the loss of /r/ in Khmer: a new tonogenetic mechanism?
scope: Phnom Penh colloquial /Cr/ forms vs careful reading; two male speakers, 20 lexical items, three repetitions per style; VOT/frication, F0 at five vowel positions and F1/F2; not a universal deletion rule

title: Transliteration of Khmer Writing
scope: comparison of Khmer romanization systems and orthographic flexibility

title: Khmer-Russian practical transcription
scope: Russian practical treatment of Khmer vowels, consonants, aspiration, clusters and glottal stop
note: Secondary web reproduction citing the 1967 Cambodian geographic-name instructions, Gorgoniyev and Serdyuchenko. Use as comparator until primary scans are independently verified.

title: Fourth International Linguistics Olympiad, Individual Problems, Problem 3
scope: Bulgarian-language academic material containing Latin phonetic transcription of Khmer data

title: MekongPhon: A Large-Scale Parallel IPA Corpus for Lao and Khmer
scope: Paper reports 1,314,779 Khmer orthography–IPA sentence pairs; seed lexicon has 8,026 word–IPA entries derived from Headley (1977), with a two-author 500-entry review (99.2% sample accuracy; reviewers are proficient L2 speakers, not native speakers). Sentence pairs are generated by longest-match trie lookup over OPUS text (NLLB/Paracrawl/OpenSubtitles); held-out evaluation is dictionary-seeded and reports <2% CER under the paper's own setup, not independent sentence transcription or our gold. Candidate secondary lexical reference/diagnostic only; not blind adjudicated IPA gold. Repository snapshot f80f6c1840c4818b51e05f2e00cded4701a5b662 has no declared license/root LICENSE; SEALang license version unspecified; rights_status=UNKNOWN pending item-level verification.

title: Applying Linguistic G2P Knowledge on a Statistical Grapheme-to-phoneme Conversion in Khmer
scope: prose reports 1,350 training pairs and 350 test pairs, but Table 10 test-corpus bins sum to 356 (112+97+98+49); abstract baseline WER 69.6% conflicts with Table 10/conclusion 69.9%; preserve discrepancies pending author clarification; dataset/normalization/profile need recovery before comparison
article_license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (article only; not a statement of source-dictionary or derived-data rights)

title: Incipient tonogenesis in Phnom Penh Khmer: audio recordings, 2011
author: James Kirby
scope: 24-bit, 44.1 kHz audio of 16 Phnom Penh Khmer speakers recorded in July 2011, with segmented Praat TextGrids; the associated study contrasts reading and colloquial /CrV/ productions
limitations: Not a lexical-wide IPA gold corpus; TextGrids provide segmentation rather than independent IPA labels; the study targets /CrV/ contexts and a historical speaker sample, not the complete contemporary citation-form lexicon. Keep reading and colloquial conditions separate.

title: Incipient tonogenesis in Phnom Penh Khmer: supplementary materials, 2011
author: James Kirby
scope: Anonymised production and perception CSVs, KlattGrid stimulus files, Praat-related measurements and R analysis code accompanying the Phnom Penh /r/-loss study
limitations: Not a lexical IPA gold corpus and not a complete phonetic transcription dataset; CSVs are study measurements/response data, not independently double-annotated IPA. Interpret only within the source study's task and speaker scope.

title: Assessing transcription agreement: Methodological aspects
author: Catia Cucchiarini
scope: Critique of percentage agreement for phonetic transcription: all-or-none symbol matching, chance agreement and missing alignment criteria; proposes alignment and average distance using experimentally derived phonetic feature matrices
limitations: Not a Khmer-specific annotation standard or universal weight matrix; informs reporting and metric design but does not supply validated Khmer feature weights.

title: A Weighted Reliability Measure for Phonetic Transcription
journal: Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research 49(6):1391–1411
scope: Weighted reliability measure for phonetic transcription, designed to distinguish degrees of phonetic difference using principles from phonological theory; evaluated with eight coders on speech and vocalisation samples, including three adult languages
limitations: Not a language-specific Khmer feature matrix; the project's current validator does not implement this published measure. A future project metric must not be attributed to Oller and Ramsdell unless their exact algorithm is reproduced.

title: Procesy fonetyczno-fonologiczne w nieregionalnej odmianie języka khmerskiego
author: Piotr Woźnica
scope: Acoustic study of 80 native Khmer speakers from multiple Cambodian regions; examines regional phonetic/phonological variation and argues for a country-wide standard variety
limitations: The thesis warns that the sample is not statistically representative; regional coverage is uneven and the materials are selective/read-text based. It is not a Phnom Penh-only sample or a lexical IPA gold corpus.

title: Khmer ASR Cultural Dataset, Version 3 Part 1
author: Digital Divide Data (DDD-Cambodia)
scope: 134.60 hours of manually curated Khmer speech-text recordings; Part 1 metadata reports 8 Cambodia-based native speakers (4 female, 4 male), 13 topics and 401 subtopics; speaker origin-city metadata is provided. WAV audio and orthographic transcripts; CC BY-SA 4.0; attribution to Digital Divide Data required.
limitations: No IPA labels or phonetic adjudication are supplied. Speaker origin city does not by itself establish a Phnom Penh phonological profile. Use only after selecting profile and filtering speaker/recording metadata; preserve utterance and word-span locators; do not attempt speaker identification. Share-alike obligations and redistribution of any derived IPA must be reviewed before publication.

title: Common Voice Scripted Speech 27.0 — Khmer
author: Mozilla Common Voice
scope: CC0-1.0 read-speech audio; 739 clips / 0.98h total, 213 validated clips / 0.28h validated, 15 speakers, 4,971 text sentences; only 364 sentences validated. Accent values absent for the reported subset; gender unreported for all speakers. Provider forbids speaker identification and re-hosting/re-sharing.
limitations: No IPA labels. Accent/variety is not established, so the data cannot be assumed to represent Phnom Penh or Standard Khmer. Most clips are unresolved/invalidated (483 unresolved, 43 invalidated); only 213 are validated. Use provider-hosted audio and opaque clip/time locators only; do not identify speakers or mirror/re-share files. Specialist profile screening and blind double annotation/adjudication remain required.

title: open-dict-data/ipa-dict — Khmer km.txt
scope: 3,286-line Khmer orthography-to-IPA lexicon in tab-separated format. Repository README attributes Khmer data to extraction from the Khmer-English Dictionary at aakanee.com.
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for the third-party Khmer data as identified in the upstream Credits; repository-wide MIT license does not override third-party data terms.
limitations: Not project gold or independent double annotation. Exact dialect/profile, transcription convention, source entry locators, and duplicate/alternative-reading handling require further review. Non-commercial/share-alike terms make this unsuitable for an unrestricted commercial release. Do not import or redistribute until compatibility with project purpose and obligations is reviewed.

title: PhonSobon Khmer G2P — Khmer Dictionary 2022 derived word-to-pronunciation pairs
scope: 38,629 word-to-pronunciation pairs (37,755 unique words) with 34,770 train, 1,939 validation and 1,920 test rows; word-level split groups all readings of a word. Pronunciation is NCKL Khmer-script respelling with syllable boundaries, not IPA. Derived from the Khmer Dictionary 2022 of the National Council of Khmer Language, Royal Academy of Cambodia.
limitations: Useful as a structural/syllabification research comparator only after rights and profile review. The dataset card says source content remains © NCKL and commercial terms must be checked; no independent open redistribution permission is established by the dataset card. Cleaning includes removed rows and source corrections. Do not treat as IPA gold, import as pronunciation gold, or infer IPA mechanically.

title: PhonSobon Khmer pronunciation dictionary (combined)
scope: 39,110 Khmer word-to-pronunciation-respelling rows; combined from Khmer Dictionary 2022-derived sources. Dataset card documents 689 disputed words with review decisions (650 judge decisions and 39 Claude-assisted confirmations requiring native-speaker confirmation).
limitations: Not IPA. Review provenance includes automated/LLM-assisted decisions and explicitly calls for native-speaker confirmation; not independent expert IPA adjudication. Source content is stated as research-only/non-commercial; do not import into a commercial or redistributable gold corpus without permission and source-level rights review.

title: Khmer Acoustic Model for Montreal Forced Aligner
scope: Upstream README claims 29,204 IPA dictionary entries validated by native Khmer linguists and declares CC BY-SA 4.0 for the pronunciation dictionary. The repository tree exposes only a six-line sample dictionary, not the claimed full dictionary. The dictionary README separately declares CC BY 4.0 for a mapping derived from 33,091 entries; artifact counts and data-license statements are not reconciled.
license: Unresolved: root README says CC BY-SA 4.0 for pronunciation dictionary; dictionary README says CC BY 4.0 for a G2P mapping; code LICENSE is MIT but does not resolve third-party data terms.
limitations: Do not import sample or claim full dictionary access. Request versioned full artifact and SHA-256, artifact-specific licenses, provenance, dialect/IPA convention, annotation/adjudication details, and release/DOI. Alignment boundary metrics are not phonetic accuracy.

title: Report on the activities of the standardization of geographical names for the period 2019–2022
scope: Cambodia reports that the national romanized writing system is based on the 1997 transcription system instead of the 1972 transliteration system; the 2019 national gazetteer used the 1997 system.
limitations: This report identifies the system and its 2019 gazetteer use but does not reproduce the full table; the primary 1995/1997 table was later located in the 2023 provisional Gazetteer (pp. vii–viii).

title: Current status of United Nations romanization systems for geographical names
scope: UNGEGN Working Group records that Cambodia's national report confirms the 1997 Khmer transcription system replaced the 1972 system and says the group will discuss its presentation to UNGEGN.
limitations: The Working Group notes the system had not yet been presented for UNGEGN official consideration/adoption.

title: Report of the Asia South-East Division
scope: Confirms that the October 2023 Cambodian General Department of Cadastre and Geography gazetteer lists Khmer and Latin geographical names using Transcription system 1997.
limitations: Corroborates the 2023 Gazetteer's use of Transcription system 1997; the primary table is in the Gazetteer itself. PCGN May 2026 describes the scheme as not yet consistently implemented, so formal adoption remains unverified.

title: Gazetteer of Cambodia, Ministry of Land Management, Urban Planning and Construction
scope: Official Ministry Gazetteer, Khmer/Latin geographical names; contains the primary 1995/1997 Khmer romanization table and foreword on provisional use.
limitations: Original PDF copyright © 2023 by Geography Department. Open Development Cambodia mirror record states no license is given for the PDF. Foreword says the system is used by the Geography Department and is to be submitted for consideration/adoption; edition is provisional pending National Commission approval.
source_locator: 2023 edition, pp. vii–viii: Romanized System for Khmer; foreword pp. iv–v states departmental use and provisional status

title: Khmer Romanization Table, 1997 version (ALA-LC)
scope: ALA-LC Khmer cataloguing romanization table, included as a comparator only.
limitations: This is a distinct ALA-LC cataloguing profile and is not evidence of Cambodia's national 1997 transcription system; do not substitute or conflate the two.

title: Cambodia Toponymic Factfile
scope: PCGN geographical names policy and status of Cambodia's 1995/1997 Khmer romanization system; describes the 1997 modification as not yet consistently implemented and records the 2025 gazetteer dataset.
limitations: PCGN assesses consistent implementation/adoption; Cambodia's reports and the provisional 2023 Gazetteer document departmental/gazetteer use. These claims may be compatible as different implementation scopes. Formal National Commission approval and reuse rights remain unverified.

title: BYU MATRIX Lab Khmer IPA model
scope: 33.6M-parameter BERT encoder-decoder with separate Khmer and IPA tokenizers; model card reports best evaluation loss 0.1736 at checkpoint 26000; the model card's example output is IPA-like. The LREC 2026 MekongPhon paper reports under 2% CER on its own held-out evaluation setup. The associated MekongPhon paper reports 1,314,779 sentence pairs expanded by longest-match lexicon lookup over OPUS from an 8,026-entry seed lexicon; 500 seed entries were reviewed by two proficient L2 speakers, not native annotators.
license: Apache-2.0 as declared by the model card
limitations: The model card license does not resolve rights in the training corpus; MekongPhon repository snapshot has no declared root LICENSE. Source-attested diagnostic results are not independent project gold; model evaluation uses pron_no_tones and does not establish tone/phonation recovery. Published under-2% CER is dictionary-seeded and not independent sentence transcription; reviewer qualifications are L2, not native target-variety adjudicators. The optional benchmark workflow is manual-dispatch only until the MekongPhon corpus license is clarified; the one-time run is retained as historical diagnostic evidence.

title: PhonSobon Khmer G2P (NCKL respelling)
scope: 7.46M-parameter character-level Transformer that predicts NCKL Khmer-script respelling with hyphenated syllable boundaries. The model card reports 83.37% validation word accuracy at epoch 150; this is an upstream validation claim, not a result independently reproduced by this repository.
license: MIT as declared by the model card; this model license does not grant rights to the underlying NCKL-derived training data.
limitations: Output is Khmer-script respelling, not IPA or a typed phonetic result, and must not enter the IPA-first runtime path. The linked dataset derives from the NCKL Khmer Dictionary 2022; its dataset card uses the nckl-khmer-dictionary-2022 license identifier, requests NCKL attribution and says to check NCKL terms before commercial use. No dataset rows or model weights are copied into this repository. No test-set score is stated in the model card.

title: PhonSobon Khmer G2P dataset (derived from NCKL Khmer Dictionary 2022)
scope: 38,629 word-to-pronunciation pairs and 37,755 unique words; published split counts are train 34,770, validation 1,939 and test 1,920. Labels are Khmer-script pronunciation respellings with hyphenated syllable boundaries, not IPA. The dataset card describes a word-level split keeping all readings of a word together.
license: Dataset card identifies nckl-khmer-dictionary-2022; it attributes content to the National Council of Khmer Language (NCKL), Royal Academy of Cambodia, requests NCKL credit and says to check NCKL terms before commercial use. Exact redistribution and derivative-use permissions remain unverified.
limitations: Standard NCKL/Phnom Penh prescribed word pronunciations; not regional or colloquial variants and not running-speech sandhi. This is a respelling/syllabification resource, not a source of IPA labels or an independent phonetic gold set. Do not redistribute or use commercially until NCKL terms are clarified; no rows are imported.

title: Khmer Pronunciation Dictionary / Khmer acoustic model
scope: The upstream root README advertises a 29,204-entry IPA dictionary; the inspected dictionary/README.md reports 33,091 entries. The pinned repository tree exposed only dictionary/khmer_ipa_sample.dict (144 bytes), not the advertised full dictionary. Reported MAE/F1 values concern forced-alignment boundaries, not G2P or IPA transcription accuracy.
license: Conflicting upstream declarations: root README says pronunciation dictionary CC BY-SA 4.0; dictionary/README.md says CC BY 4.0. Code/model MIT terms do not resolve third-party dictionary-data rights.
limitations: Do not import, benchmark or redistribute the six-entry sample as if it represented the full lexicon. Require a versioned complete dictionary and digest, reconciled entry count, item-level provenance, dialect/IPA convention and authoritative data-license clarification. Native-linguist validation is an upstream claim, not independently verified here.

title: Google Language Resources — Khmer TTS lexicon and phonology inventory
scope: Full-file audit of archived Google Language Resources km/data/lexicon.tsv at pinned repository commit a90601024f07ab7e96c911243324e0adeb16da96 (blob d399efeca642b1185786b2982374488c525e37c4; GitHub reports 2.71 MB): 69,415 two-column rows and 69,405 unique spellings (62,175 Khmer-script and 7,230 Latin-script). Ten spelling keys occur twice and each pair has divergent phonemic transcriptions; although the header describes an optional third disambiguating column, every row has only two columns. The lexicon uses 54 distinct phonemic tokens, all present in km/festvox/phonology.json (56 inventory phones: 30 vowels, 24 consonants, 2 silence; sil and pau are unused). The notation is a project-specific phonemic inventory, including ASCII digraphs and doubled-vowel length labels, not a documented strict IPA convention. The companion Festival prompt file km/festvox/txt.done.data (blob 01ca58b32544bcfd44305b91931baf192cce287d) contains 2,748 utterance records across 16 pseudonymous speaker-ID prefixes; it has no gender labels and is not an archive manifest. This is 158 fewer records and one fewer speaker than the paper's 2,906/17 table, so the repository snapshot does not reconcile the published or current OpenSLR archive counts. The 2018 paper reports 70,671 Khmer entries, 1,256 more than the pinned snapshot. It says source words were crawled from Wikipedia/websites, frequency-ranked, manually transcribed by linguists using guidelines and QC'd, but supplies no Khmer-specific guideline, target dialect, per-item source locators, annotator count or error rate.
license: The km/data/lexicon.tsv header explicitly declares CC BY 4.0. The companion km/festvox/phonology.json and km/festvox/txt.done.data have no file-level license header; the repository README says original files are Apache-2.0 unless otherwise noted, while the 2018 paper broadly says all data are CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise noted. Treat the lexicon file as CC BY 4.0; the exact license scope for the companion phonology JSON remains unresolved pending clarification.
limitations: Candidate lexical/phonemic comparator only, not independent IPA gold or an accuracy benchmark. The lexicon includes Khmer-script and Latin-script keys but does not identify target variety; its phonemic convention is not documented as standard IPA and does not encode tone/register. Preserve all ten divergent duplicate spellings as alternatives; the optional disambiguation labels described in the header are absent from the actual two-column rows. The 70,671 paper count differs from the 69,415-row snapshot and requires version clarification. No per-entry source locators or item-level provenance are supplied. The 2,748-row Festival prompt file is not a complete audio manifest and does not identify speaker gender or reconcile the 2,906-file/17-speaker paper table. Do not derive the project’s Phnom Penh careful-citation profile or gold labels from these entries without specialist review and independent annotation.

title: OpenSLR SLR42 — High quality TTS data for Khmer
scope: OpenSLR currently lists one 866 MB archive, km_kh_male.zip, described as male-speaker Khmer speech with audio and a TSV of orthographic transcriptions. The 2018 Sodimana et al. paper reports 17 female speakers, 2,906 audio files and 3:58:00 for Khmer. The pinned Google repository's km/festvox/txt.done.data is a separate Festival prompt index with 2,748 rows and 16 speaker-ID prefixes (no gender labels), also differing from the paper's 2,906 files/17 speakers; it is not a checksum-backed archive manifest. This is a material archive/paper/repository metadata discrepancy requiring manifest-level reconciliation.
license: The current OpenSLR SLR42 page and its linked LICENSE file both declare CC BY-SA 4.0. The 2018 paper reports a general CC BY 4.0 data release unless otherwise noted, so the provider's current archive-specific CC BY-SA declaration takes precedence for the currently listed archive pending clarification of historical versions. The linked license was inspected; the 866 MB archive's internal copy was not downloaded or inspected.
limitations: The corpus contains audio plus Khmer text transcripts, not word-level IPA labels or independent phonetic gold. Do not infer that the currently listed male archive is the same speaker set as the paper's 17-female-speaker table. Obtain and inspect the exact archive manifest, checksum, speaker IDs and license before annotation or derivative use.

title: MekongPhon rule-based Khmer-to-IPA baseline
scope: Experimental rule-based baseline with consonant/register and vowel assignment tables and Khmer tokenization; distinct from the BYU MATRIX neural encoder-decoder. Source code was inspected but not executed by this project.
license: The pinned MekongPhon repository snapshot has no declared root LICENSE. Do not copy or redistribute source code/data pending rights clarification.
limitations: Output conventions, dialect/profile coverage, tokenization behavior and compatibility with the project's typed IPA contract have not been validated. Not an enabled provider, not gold, and not a source of empirical accuracy.

title: The Syllabic and Morphological Structure of Cambodian Words
author: Karnchana Nacaskul
scope: Describes major and minor syllables. For major syllables it reports no final consonant clusters, a listed coda inventory, and no short vowels/short diphthongs in open syllables. It separately defines minor type A (clusters only with /r/ in second position; short /ə/ or /ɔ/; no coda) and type B (single onset; restricted short nucleus; coda among four nasals).
limitations: 1978 description using its own transcription and register analysis. Do not treat minor-type restrictions as global phonotactic bans or assume every coda inventory detail is current for the selected Phnom Penh careful-citation profile. Reconcile with contemporary acoustic/lexical evidence before encoding rules.

title: Khmer Encoding Structure (L2/22-290)
author: Martin Hosken, with Norbert Lindenberg and Makara Sok
scope: Describes modern Khmer orthographic syllable structure as a base plus up to two pre-vowel coengs and an optional dependent vowel; documents coeng use for initial clusters and syllable chaining, and notes that phonetic syllable count can differ from orthographic units. It distinguishes Middle Khmer final coengs from modern dictionary orthography and notes personal-name exceptions.
limitations: This is an encoding/orthography proposal, not a phonological grammar. The two-coeng limit is not a statement that Khmer has at most two onset consonants; chaining can place a previous phonetic coda inside the next orthographic unit.

title: Statistical Khmer Name Romanization
author: Chenchen Ding, Vichet Chea, Masao Utiyama, Eiichiro Sumita, Sethserey Sam, Sopheap Seng
scope: Reports two-consonant onset clusters as common, three as the maximum, and roughly 80 possible consonant combinations. Based on a 7,658-instance Khmer personal-name romanization/alignment study; explicitly discusses mismatch between phonemic syllables and orthographic unbreakable writing units, including silent etymological stacked letters and syllable chaining.
license: The paper states that its manually aligned name-romanization data were released under CC BY-NC-SA for research use; exact current hosting and file-level terms must be checked before reuse.
limitations: A name-romanization/NLP study, not an exhaustive phonological field survey. The approximate 80 cluster types and three-consonant maximum are secondary descriptive claims, not an authoritative exhaustive list or a basis for rejecting individual clusters. No dataset rows are imported.

title: Phonologization of Pitch in Phnom Penh and Standard Khmer for Cluster and Disyllabic Words
author: Sothornin Mam, Pittayawat Pittayaporn, Sireemas Maspong
scope: Compares Standard Khmer and Phnom Penh Khmer using 50 target words, five native speakers (two male, three female), and three repetitions. F0 was measured in the stressed rime. The study reports a lower F0 group for /r>h/ forms and for voiced-onset disyllables in PPK, suggesting that pitch may be phonologizing beyond the previously described /r/-loss context.
limitations: The paper describes the result as possible/incipient phonologization and calls for further study. It is a bounded wordlist and five-speaker sample, not a complete perception study or an independently adjudicated project gold set. Do not add a general Khmer tone rule or infer tone from orthography alone.

title: Cambodian: An Essential Grammar
author: Chhany Sak-Humphry
scope: Publisher preview excerpt discusses CVF and CCVF syllable patterns, short/long nuclei and final consonants. The retrieved excerpt states that short or long vowels are possible when a final is present and that open monosyllables require a long nucleus.
limitations: The retrieved preview excerpt lists /r/ among permitted finals and then also lists /r/ among excluded finals. Do not use this excerpt to settle the coda inventory until the full text or an author/publisher correction resolves the contradiction.

title: Cataloging Service Bulletin No. 43 (Winter 1989), Khmer Romanization
scope: Historical Library of Congress Khmer romanization notes; page 54, Note 10 describes romanization word division using the shortest written form that can stand alone as a word, including Pali and Sanskrit loan-words, while other loan-words retain original-language divisions.
limitations: This is a 1989 policy snapshot, not proof that the same wording remains the current ALA-LC rule. Compare the 1997 ALA-LC table's Note 10 and the 2013 table's Note 8 before implementing a versioned profile.

title: Khmer Romanization Table, 2013 version (ALA-LC)
scope: Current surfaced ALA-LC Khmer cataloguing table; Note 8 says Khmer words are not written separately and any word can be separated when romanizing; Pali/Sanskrit loans follow the same rule, while other loans are divided according to their original language.
limitations: This is a distinct ALA-LC profile, not BGN/PCGN 1972 or Cambodia's national 1995/1997 system. The note does not supply a lexical segmentation algorithm, dictionary, boundary annotations or deterministic treatment of ambiguous compounds.

title: Unicode Technical Note #61: Khmer Encoding Structure, Version 2
author: Martin Hosken
scope: Non-normative technical analysis of Modern Khmer encoding and orthographic-syllable structure, including coengs, consonant shifters, vowel/sign ordering, canonical equivalence, deprecated/discouraged sequences, and shaping. Used only as background for a separately versioned Modern Khmer profile.
license: Unicode Terms of Use apply. Public reproduction, modification, or distribution beyond permitted personal/internal use requires permission unless specifically licensed. This registry records source metadata only and does not reproduce the PDF text or regular expressions.
limitations: Unicode Technical Notes are independently prepared, are not part of the Unicode Standard or a Unicode specification, and do not imply UTC or Unicode Consortium endorsement. The note is an encoding proposal/analysis, not a universal phonological grammar or a replacement for Unicode 18 §16.4. No TN #61-derived grammar is implemented by the current parser; any future use must be a separately versioned profile with independent review. Verify that version 2 remains current before future implementation.
